source.title: Beyond the Mean: Fisher-Orthogonal Projection for Natural Gradient Descent in Large Batch Training

record.file_problem: The supplied text includes the full paper and supplementary material. Some equations and table formatting are flattened, but the relevant Table 1 entries can be assigned to methods and batch sizes.
record.tranche_reason: Tests large-batch effects on test performance with a new optimizer comparison and reports CIFAR-10 test-accuracy threshold results.
record.gate_note: The study reports test accuracy over time and epochs/time to reach a test-accuracy threshold, but does not directly measure the train–test gap. Other benchmark comparisons are not extracted as evidence about the claim unless they report a relevant test-performance result.
record.test_reason: The study varies batch size and measures held-out accuracy under fixed epoch budgets, testing V5 with different optimizers. A train–test gap is unnecessary for V5, which concerns held-out performance.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is broadly accurate. The authors claim that FOP improves large-batch scalability and convergence while preserving small-batch accuracy, and improves long-tailed CIFAR error rates. They explicitly avoid claiming universal optimizer superiority. Threshold attainment supports scalability, but alone does not establish equal final accuracy across batch sizes.
record.recipe_differences: Uses standard image-classification training with tuned optimizer schedules and batch-size-scaled learning rates; compares a new natural-gradient optimizer against SGD, AdamW, and KFAC. Reports threshold attainment and time-to-threshold rather than direct train–test gaps.
record.method_sensitivity: Batch size changes threshold attainment; optimizer choice changes whether the threshold is reached. The paper also reports sensitivity to damping ratio, but those figure-only sweeps do not directly measure the version's batch-size effect.

fits_no_version.finding: FOP reduces test error relative to KFAC and published baselines on long-tailed CIFAR datasets.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Fisher-orthogonal correction improves classification accuracy under class imbalance.

record.problems: The study does not report train error alongside test error, so the generalization gap itself cannot be assessed. The selected results are threshold attainment and time-to-threshold, and the text does not report uncertainty for the table entries.
record.rows_left_out: Other optimizer and batch-size entries in Table 1 and Tables 2–3 were not extracted because the selected CIFAR-10 rows already capture the reported contrast across moderate and very large batches. Figure-only accuracy curves were not converted into values.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting compared with natural-label generalization.
Convolutional versus fully connected architectural comparisons.
Whether adaptive optimizers have worse held-out performance than SGD under limited tuning; time to a shared threshold does not establish that comparison.

Language models; longer-training interventions; isolated effects of warmup, normalization, and regularization. The extracted threshold rows do not establish equal final accuracy or complete elimination of a batch-size penalty with FOP.
Magnitude-aware sharpness rankings and their correlation with generalization gaps.
Removal of memorized examples versus random removal.

record.verdict_notes: Other batch entries, Tables 2–3, and figure-only accuracy curves are already declared omitted in rows_left_out. The study reports five seeds for CIFAR-10, although Table 1 provides no uncertainty. Its sharp-minimum explanation is not a test of V7.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Width sweeps beyond the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected architecture comparisons.
Adaptive versus SGD generalization under different tuning budgets.
Language models; equal-epoch final-accuracy comparisons across all methods and batch sizes; longer training and the specific warmup, normalization, or regularization changes listed in the version.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and other generalization measures.
Removing memorized examples and measuring the resulting test-accuracy change.

relationships.display_finding: SGD, AdamW and KFAC reached 91% test accuracy at batch 2048 but failed to reach it at batches 32768 and 50000 within 100 epochs.
